reason: Under EBS volume usage, the quote states that while an interrupted Spot Instance is stopped you are charged only for the preserved EBS volumes.

The claim drops a condition of the second quote: EC2 restarts the stopped instance in the same AZ and instance type only when the same launch specification is used; the quotes do support that only EC2 can restart it.
The Available capacity row states the Spot request keeps making the launch request until capacity is available, while an On-Demand launch gets an insufficient capacity error (ICE).

The decision-guide quote gives exactly this general guideline: Spot for flexible interruption-tolerant variable work, Savings Plans for steady-state predictable work needing uninterrupted availability.
The Elastic IP row says it remains associated for reboot, stop/start and hibernate, and is disassociated on terminate.
The Host computer row says reboot stays on the same host; stop/start and hibernate move to a new host though in some cases it remains on the current host.
The Instance store volumes row says data is preserved on reboot and erased on stop/start, hibernate and terminate.
The Private IPv4 row says the instance keeps it for reboot, stop/start and hibernate, and None for terminate.
The Public IPv4 row states the reboot behavior and the stop/start and hibernate behavior with the same Elastic IP exception, word for word.
The RAM row says RAM is erased on reboot, stop/start and terminate, and saved to a file on the root volume only for hibernate.
The Root volume row says the volume is preserved for reboot, stop/start and hibernate and deleted by default on terminate.
The pending row describes preparing to enter running after a launch or a start from stopped, with billing Not billed.
The running row says the instance is running and ready for use, with billing Billed.
The shutting-down row says the instance is preparing to be terminated, with billing Not billed.
The stopped row says the instance is shut down, cannot be used, can be started at any time, and instance usage is Not billed.
The stopping row says Not billed, except that a hibernating instance is billed while in the stopping state.
The terminated row says permanently deleted, cannot be started, Not billed, and RIs that applied are billed until the end of their term per payment option.
The quotes say instance status checks monitor software and network connectivity of the instance and detect problems needing your involvement, for example rebooting or configuration changes.
The quote states system checks monitor the AWS systems, detect problems needing AWS involvement, and for EBS-backed instances a stop and start in most cases migrates the instance to a new host.
The quote states status checks are performed every minute, returning a pass or a fail status.

The two quotes name the four types, say system, instance and attached EBS checks are EC2-managed, run on every instance and cannot be disabled, and that application checks are opt-in and monitor HTTP or HTTPS responses.
Under Steady-state workloads, the quote says consistent predictable applications such as databases and core infrastructure benefit most from long-term commitments through Savings Plans.
The two quotes state stop protection cannot be enabled for an instance with an instance store root volume or for Spot Instances.

The claim drops the condition on Auto Scaling: the quote says stop protection does not prevent Auto Scaling termination when the instance is unhealthy or during scale-in events, not Auto Scaling termination in general; the rest is supported.
The quote says that if an instance fails a status check and its root volume is EBS, you can stop and start it to try to fix the problem.
The quote states a started instance moves to a new host (in some cases it stays) and data on instance store volumes of the previous host is lost.
The Billing row states reboot keeps the billing hour, stop/start charges stop at stopping, hibernate charges stop at stopped, and each start begins a new period with a one-minute minimum.
The quote says a stopped instance is not charged for usage, EBS storage is charged, and certain attributes including the instance type can be modified.
The pricing quote says partial instance-hours are billed per second for Linux, Windows, RHEL and Ubuntu Pro, and SLES instances are billed as a full hour.
The quotes say tenancy can be changed after launch on a stopped instance, the instance must be stopped, not via the console, and the change takes effect at next start.
The quote says a terminated instance stays visible in the console for a short while, the entry is then deleted automatically, and you cannot connect to or recover it.
The quote states that with termination protection enabled you cannot terminate the instance using the console, CLI, or API.
The quotes say termination protection is disabled by default and does not prevent scheduled-event termination by AWS or Auto Scaling termination when unhealthy or during scale-in.
Under Unpredictable bursts, the quote says such systems benefit from maximum flexibility through On-Demand or Spot capacity.
The quote states user data is limited to 16 KB in raw form before base64 encoding.
The quote says user data is an instance attribute and is not included in an AMI created from the instance.
Under the Linux shell scripts heading, the quote says user data scripts run as root, so do not use sudo.
The quote states the first-launch default; the next sentence in context says the configuration can be updated to run at every restart.

The quotes say user data is specified at launch, can be updated after a stop when the root volume is EBS, and updated user data does not run automatically at start; the Windows exception is in the qualifiers.
The FAQ answer to whether vCPU limits apply when purchasing RIs is no; they apply only to running On-Demand and Spot Instances.
